props.gloss_en: the mishna: [a convert's cow slaughtered] in doubt [whether before or after he converted] -- exempt
Reish Lakish: we learned 'in doubt, exempt' -- evidently a doubt [here] is ruled leniently
ant holes within the standing crop belong to the householder; those behind the harvesters -- the upper [grain] to the poor and the lower to the householder
R' Meir: all to the poor, for a doubt of leket is leket
R' Yochanan: do not provoke me -- I teach it in the language of a single [sage]
a doubt of leket is leket, a doubt of shikhecha is shikhecha, a doubt of pe'ah is pe'ah

Reish Lakish: what is 'do justice to the poor and destitute' (Ps 82:3)? if in judgments -- but it is written 'nor favour a poor man in his cause' (Ex 23:3)! rather: be righteous with what is yours and give him
Rava: here, the cow stands in a presumption of exemption
Rava: the standing crop stands in a presumption of obligation
Abaye: but dough -- made before he converted, exempt from challa; after he converted, obligated; in doubt, obligated
Rava: a doubt of prohibition -- stringently
Rava: a doubt of money -- leniently
eight doubts were said of the convert: four for obligation and four for exemption
his wife's offering, challa, the firstborn of an impure animal and the firstborn of a pure animal -- for obligation
the first shearing, the gifts, the redemption of the son and the redemption of the firstborn donkey -- for exemption
Ravin: he [Reish Lakish] raised standing crop against standing crop
Levi sowed in Kishar and there were no poor to take leket; he came before Rav Sheshet
Rav Sheshet: 'for the poor and the stranger you shall leave them' (Lev 23:22) -- and not for ravens nor for bats
one does not bring teruma from threshing floor to town or from wilderness to settlement; and if there is no priest there, he hires a cow and brings it, because of the loss of teruma
teruma is different: it renders [the crop] tevel, and there is no way but to separate it

where they are accustomed to scald calves, one does not skin the foreleg; [where] to skin the head, one does not skin the jaw; and if there is no priest, they are valued and he eats them, because of the priest's loss
priestly gifts are different: 'giving' is written of them
now that you have come to this -- teruma too: 'giving' is written of it
one who renounces his vineyard and at dawn rose and harvested it -- obligated in peret, olelot, shikhecha and pe'ah, and exempt from tithes
a certain sack of dinars came to the study hall; R' Ami was first and acquired them
it is written 'and he shall give' -- and not that he take by himself
R' Ami too acquired them for the poor
or say: an important person is different
'and the priest who is greater than his brethren' (Lev 21:10) -- that he be greater than his brethren in beauty, in wisdom and in wealth
Others: from where that if he has none, his brethren the priests make him great? 'the priest who is greater than his brethren' -- make him great from what is his brethren's
